records.reason: m190 at 2/1 and 100 uL fills the gap between its measured 1/1 and 10/1 conditions. Its recent pure-EA result rejected transfer of a late-onset anomaly from the positional isomer; this label constrains the remaining local response curve.

m186 at 20/1 and 150 uL supplies a loading contrast to the measured 100 uL condition and pairs with the selected 50/1 point. It tests whether onset and completion change differently as EA becomes scarce.

m186 at 50/1 and 150 uL completes the selected high-loading 20/1-to-50/1 segment. Comparison with its measured low-loading 50/1 result can localize loading associations independently of the exceptional low-loading pure-EA observation.

Terephthalaldehyde m191 at 5/1 and 50 uL starts a fixed-loading 5/1-to-10/1 experiment. Existing 100 uL measurements show substantial growth across this segment, making the lower-loading curve useful for learning endpoint-specific transitions.

m191 at 10/1 and 50 uL completes that fixed-loading segment and contrasts with the measured 100 uL result of approximately 27.27/61.62 mL. It tests whether onset and completion transfer together across loading.

Methyl anthranilate at 1/1 and 50 uL tests the localization of the measured onset difference between 100 and 150 uL. Together with selected 2/1 and 5/1 points, it determines whether an early-ratio onset maximum recurs at lower loading.

Methyl anthranilate at 2/1 and 50 uL is the central point of the selected 1/1-to-5/1 curve. Its prediction is approximately 4.62/10.98 mL; measurement will distinguish a real local response reversal from overtransfer of individual loading records.

Methyl anthranilate at 5/1 and 50 uL connects the selected early-ratio points to its measured low-loading 20/1 condition. The latest short 50/1 result weakens transfer of ethyl anthranilate's large weak-eluent response to this methyl ester.
p-Methoxyacetophenone at 1/1 and 50 uL supplies the missing lower-loading counterpart to measured 100 and 150 uL baselines. It anchors a fixed-loading comparison with the selected 10/1 condition.

p-Methoxyacetophenone at 10/1 and 50 uL tests the approximately 13.69/30.49 mL forecast. The measured 100 uL 10/1 endpoints were shorter than its 5/1 endpoints, so this point discriminates loading dependence from a localized ratio reversal.

p-Methylthioacetophenone at 2/1 and 100 uL fills the gap between its recently measured 1/1 baseline and established 5/1 response. It tests the early transition in the ketone without transferring the sulfur-containing aldehyde's shorter response.

Dimethyl-substituted benzophenone m131 at 20/1 and 100 uL precedes its measured 50/1 result, which retained an early onset with later completion. This tests whether completion growth develops while onset remains nearly stationary.

p-Methoxybenzophenone at 10/1 and 100 uL fills the interval before its measured 20/1 response. Comparison with the selected dimethylbenzophenone point constrains how aromatic substitution and connectivity relate to onset and completion, without assuming a controlled substitution effect.
1-Tetralone at 20/1 fills a ratio gap between measured 5/1 and 50/1 conditions. The approximately 12.05/28.84 mL forecast tests where this cyclic aromatic ketone begins its larger response.

The larger-ring aromatic ketone m179 at 10/1 connects its measured 5/1 and 50/1 conditions. Together with the tetralone selection, it provides related ring environments for learning scaffold-specific transition locations.

Naphthyl methyl ketone m40 at 50/1 and 150 uL tests loading transfer from the measured 50 uL result of approximately 40.62/65.53 mL. Its forecast of 26.74/49.67 mL could reflect substantial shrinkage toward related ketones.

m40 at 10/1 and 150 uL anchors the same loading used in the selected 50/1 condition. It separates loading-associated changes from late-ratio curvature and connects to the measured 20/1 middle-loading result.

Dibenzoylmethane at 50/1 and 50 uL tests the approximately 10.49/28.56 mL forecast against high-loading records with onset near 5 mL. This can reveal whether loading primarily changes onset while completion remains similar.

Benzoylacetone at 50/1 and 50 uL supplies a related diketone loading contrast to its measured 100 uL result of 15.40/34.50 mL. The pair of diketone selections tests whether loading associations transfer across their different carbonyl environments.

The dibenzoyl-substituted arene m178 at 2/1 adds an early anchor before measured 5/1, 10/1 and 20/1 conditions. Existing records suggest completion grows before onset rises sharply; this label tests the beginning of that endpoint decoupling.

Benzyl benzoate at 50/1 and 100 uL fills a loading gap near measured 50/1 and 100/1 low-loading anchors. It tests whether the model's intermediate-loading prediction preserves the onset and completion relationships of this aromatic ester.

Diethyl phenylmalonate at 10/1 and 150 uL fills the high-loading curve before its measured 20/1 conditions. Low-loading 10/1 completion is near 19 mL, while the forecast is 23.86 mL; the label tests completion-specific loading transfer.

Iodophenol at 10/1 and 150 uL fills the missing point before its measured high-loading 20/1-to-50/1 growth. Comparing with the recent 50 uL 10/1 result tests whether the onset-associated loading contrast already appears here.

Iodophenol at 20/1 and 100 uL fills the loading midpoint between measured 50 and 150 uL conditions. Those endpoints differ much more in onset than completion, so the midpoint directly tests that recorded association.

Iodophenol at 2/1 and 150 uL connects its measured 1/1 baseline to later-ratio growth. This constrains the high-loading transition before 10/1 and prevents the recently established weak-eluent response from inducing a uniform shift.

Naphthylethanol under pure EA at 150 uL anchors the strong-eluent boundary before measured 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1 endpoints rise substantially. It tests where the alcohol scaffold's strong retention begins and limits extrapolation across aromatic alcohols.

Bromodimethoxybenzene m108 at 20/1 and 150 uL fills a high-loading gap between measured 10/1 and 50/1 references. Its measured low-loading 20/1 condition provides a loading comparison in a donor-free ether environment.

3-Phenylpropanol at 1/1 and 50 uL fills the lower-loading curve before its measured 2/1 condition. It tests whether the loading-associated onset differences seen at later ratios are already present near the strong-eluent boundary.

The bicyclic acrylate m23 at 5/1 and 150 uL has predicted V2 below V1, approximately 5.81 versus 6.42 mL. Measuring this tuple directly tests an endpoint-ordering failure in a short-retention structural environment.

m23 at 20/1 and 150 uL pairs with its selected 5/1 point at fixed loading. It tests whether the predicted recovery to ordered endpoints reflects a real response curve or an artifact concentrated around the intermediate ratio.

The long-chain dibromothiophene m71 under pure EA at 100 uL anchors a fixed-loading comparison with its selected 10/1 condition. It extends learning to a lipophilic scaffold with weak conventional hydrogen-bonding interactions.

m71 at 10/1 and 100 uL completes that fixed-loading comparison. The predictor decreases onset while increasing completion relative to pure EA; labels can determine whether this modest endpoint decoupling is reproducible outside the polar families.

hypotheses.content: Loading associations depend on molecule and PE/EA and can affect onset and completion differently. Recent mandelate and aromatic-alcohol measurements support endpoint-specific associations, but missing experimental factors prevent assigning every contrast causally to loading.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many supplied predictions remain nearly insensitive to loading. Missing loading points and linked ratio measurements can teach when onset and completion should move together, separately, or very little, improving transfer across related rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the iodophenol midpoint, aromatic-ketone and diketone contrasts preserve onset-dominant loading differences, and do early-ratio aminoester and alcohol contrasts show the same association?

hypotheses.content: Response curvature and endpoint coupling require scaffold-specific structure-condition relationships. The latest iodophenol growth and methyl-anthranilate shortening show why neither a universal polarity shift nor unconditional monotonicity adequately describes every recorded curve.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels in ratio gaps can locate response transitions and distinguish onset growth from completion growth. Recorded reversals also help prevent the model from spreading a related scaffold's response into unsuitable conditions; they do not establish a universal chromatographic mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected aminoester, sulfur-ketone, benzophenone, cyclic-ketone and dialdehyde points reveal different transition locations or endpoint-specific reversals?

hypotheses.content: The late, nearly coincident low-loading m186 pure-EA endpoints do not justify a loading-invariant or positional-isomer-wide correction. Other strong-eluent measurements are ordinary, while the remaining weak-eluent curves may still differ between the isomers.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest outcomes identify inappropriate transfer of an exceptional record. A small number of remaining condition points can constrain isomer-specific curves while avoiding repeated acquisition of already established strong-eluent baselines.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m190's missing 2/1 point remain ordinary, and does m186's high-loading 20/1-to-50/1 segment resemble its lower-loading weak-eluent response?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest results substantially weakened transfer of the unusual low-loading m186 pure-EA record. Higher-loading m186 under pure EA measured 4.31/13.99 mL, and m190 under pure EA measured 3.88/19.14 mL, despite historical acquisition forecasts with onset near 21 mL. Their 1/1 results were also ordinary. I retain only a small isomer-specific condition block and move away from further nearby pure-EA baseline measurements.

Methyl anthranilate at 50/1 measured 6.84/12.43 mL against its historical 22.61/46.28 mL forecast. This strongly weakens transfer of ethyl anthranilate's large 50/1 response and motivates a lower-loading early-ratio curve that can distinguish localized onset behavior from broader aminoester retention. The predicted sulfur-aldehyde 1/1 completion maximum also failed: measured completion was 10.46 mL. The next sulfur-containing selection therefore fills the ketone's own early transition rather than assuming a common sulfur correction.

The recent mandelate and methylbenzyl-alcohol outcomes strengthen the value of endpoint-specific loading contrasts. Mandelate at 5/1 changed from 22.73/30.09 to 18.60/32.30 mL between 50 and 150 uL; methylbenzyl alcohol at 10/1 changed from 47.38/68.38 to 34.69/65.27 mL. Iodophenol likewise showed a larger loading contrast in onset than completion at 20/1. These are recorded associations, with possible unrecorded variability. The comparatively accurate recent diketone, alcohol and nonpolar-aromatic results discourage applying a blanket correction across those families. Historical forecast errors are used only as acquisition-time feedback, not as current-model residuals.
batch_rationale:
All 32 choices are distinct supplied candidate IDs. The batch combines local experiments with missing curve points that address relationships likely to recur across the Row-distribution. The methyl-anthranilate three-point curve, methoxyacetophenone pair, terephthalaldehyde pair, m186 segment and naphthyl-ketone pair distinguish loading transfer from solvent-response shape. The iodophenol selections add a loading midpoint and earlier high-loading conditions after its newly established steep weak-eluent growth. These experiments can teach endpoint-specific interactions without assuming that every measured loading contrast is causal.

The other carbonyl and ester selections fill transition gaps across sulfur ketones, benzophenones, cyclic ketones, diketones and aromatic esters. Related structures are included where they can constrain generalization, while their cross-molecule differences are not treated as controlled substitution effects. The bicyclic acrylate pair tests a concrete predicted endpoint-ordering failure. The fixed-loading dibromothiophene pair checks endpoint decoupling in a lipophilic environment, providing a useful comparison outside the polar families.

I reduce spending on additional sulfoxide, formal P/O and nitrobenzophenone strong-eluent baselines because recent measurements already localized much of their unusual behavior. Selection is not based on maximizing retention or elution interval width. Quantile widths are neither calibrated epistemic uncertainty nor a substitute for the chemical and condition-response evidence. All supplied predictions remain frozen before any new label reveal.
